# vram-fit

> vram-fit is an open-source Python CLI, library and local HTTP/WebSocket API that computes exactly how much GPU memory (VRAM) a local LLM needs — model weights, KV cache, activation buffers, CUDA/driver overhead and LoRA/QLoRA optimizer states — for a given context length, batch size, quantization (GGUF Q4_K_M/Q8_0/IQ4_XS…, EXL2, AWQ, GPTQ, FP8, NF4, MXFP4) and engine (llama.cpp, Ollama, vLLM, ExLlamaV2, Unsloth, Hugging Face PEFT), before any weights are downloaded. It reads only config.json or GGUF/safetensors headers, probes the local NVIDIA/AMD/Apple Silicon GPU, predicts tokens/s from memory bandwidth, and prints a tuned launch command that does not hit "CUDA out of memory".

Author: Azimxon Vaxobov (Ginckl) — https://azimxonvaxobov.netlify.app · https://www.linkedin.com/in/azimxon-vaxobov/ · https://t.me/A_Vakhobov

Key facts:

- Install: `pip install vram-fit` (zero dependencies, Python >= 3.9). API server: `pip install "vram-fit[server]"`.
- One-liners: `vram-fit fit <hf-repo> --gpu auto -c 32k` (best config + command), `vram-fit estimate <model> --gpu rtx-4090 -q Q4_K_M -c 32k --kv 8`, `vram-fit matrix <gguf-repo> --gpu rtx-4070`, `vram-fit fit <repo> --mode qlora --engine unsloth -c 4k`.
- Every command supports `--json` (one JSON document on stdout; schema in schema.json); exit 0 ok, 2 error, 3 with `--fail-on-oom` when it would OOM.
- Accuracy: synthesized GGUF sizes within 0.03–0.16 % of real files; KV cache identical to llama.cpp logs; LoRA trainable params identical to PEFT; ~0.26 ms per estimate.
- Solves: CUDA OOM in llama.cpp/Ollama/vLLM/Transformers, choosing a GGUF quant for 6/8/12/16/24 GB GPUs, -ngl / --n-cpu-moe / num_gpu / gpu_memory_utilization / max_model_len tuning, KV-cache size at 32k–128k context, LoRA/QLoRA/full fine-tuning memory and batch size, Apple Silicon wired-memory limits, MoE expert offload, tokens/s prediction.
- Status values: fits (<92 % of VRAM), tight (92–100 %), offload (layers/KV in RAM), spill (over VRAM), oom (over VRAM + RAM).
- Memory segments: weights, kv_cache, activations, overhead, lora_optimizer (MiB).

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/GinckL/vram-fit/blob/HEAD/README.md): TL;DR, Q&A for common VRAM questions, comparison matrix, formulas, CLI and API reference
- [Full documentation for LLMs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GinckL/vram-fit/HEAD/llms-full.txt): everything in one plain-text file, including the live CLI reference, quant and GPU preset tables
- [Agent guide](https://github.com/GinckL/vram-fit/blob/HEAD/AGENT_GUIDE.md): when and how an AI coding agent should run vram-fit with `--json`, fields to parse, recipes
- [JSON schema](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GinckL/vram-fit/HEAD/schema.json): JSON Schema of every `--json` output (estimate, fit, matrix, errors)

## CLI

- [estimate](https://github.com/GinckL/vram-fit/blob/HEAD/README.md#cli-reference): VRAM breakdown + tok/s for one configuration (`--command` adds the launch command)
- [fit](https://github.com/GinckL/vram-fit/blob/HEAD/README.md#quick-start): search quant x KV dtype x GPU layers x MoE offload x micro-batch for the best non-OOM config and print the command / Modelfile / train.py
- [matrix](https://github.com/GinckL/vram-fit/blob/HEAD/README.md#quick-start): quantization x context fit table
- [inspect, hw, presets, quants, catalog, serve](https://github.com/GinckL/vram-fit/blob/HEAD/README.md#cli-reference): metadata, hardware probe, 105 GPU presets, quant formats, offline model catalog, API server

## API

- [Python API](https://github.com/GinckL/vram-fit/blob/HEAD/README.md#python-api): `load_model`, `parse_gpu_spec`, `probe`, `estimate(model, gpu, Settings(...))`, `optimize`, `build_command`
- [HTTP + WebSocket API](https://github.com/GinckL/vram-fit/blob/HEAD/README.md#http--websocket-api): `vram-fit serve` → `/api/estimate`, `/api/optimize`, `/api/matrix`, `/api/hardware`, `/ws` (coalesced live estimates + GPU telemetry)

## Source

- [estimator.py](https://github.com/GinckL/vram-fit/blob/HEAD/src/vram_fit/estimator.py): weights / KV / activations / overhead / training-state math, GPU-RAM placement, tok/s model
- [quant.py](https://github.com/GinckL/vram-fit/blob/HEAD/src/vram_fit/quant.py): llama.cpp k-quant mixing rules and per-format byte accounting
- [gguf.py](https://github.com/GinckL/vram-fit/blob/HEAD/src/vram_fit/gguf.py): streaming GGUF header parser over HTTP Range
- [hardware.py](https://github.com/GinckL/vram-fit/blob/HEAD/src/vram_fit/hardware.py): NVML (ctypes), ROCm sysfs, Apple sysctl probing and telemetry
